question: Should OpenClaw add an enforced per-target-agent subagent concurrency setting, and should it live under `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` rather than as a new top-level agent field?
rationale: The request adds a public configuration surface whose namespace and interaction with the global lane limit determine upgrade, documentation, and runtime behavior; source evidence does not establish a pre-approved contract.

options.title: Adopt per-target subagent caps
options.body: Add a validated per-agent `subagents.maxConcurrent` contract that composes with the existing global cap and document the effective-limit rule.

options.title: Keep only the global cap
options.body: Decline the new configuration surface and document the global subagent lane as the supported concurrency boundary.

options.title: Unify it with broader lane work
options.body: Defer this narrow request until maintainers choose a single broader model for named and per-agent concurrency lanes.

recommendation.title: Adopt per-target subagent caps
recommendation.body: Add a validated per-agent `subagents.maxConcurrent` contract that composes with the existing global cap and document the effective-limit rule.

likelyOwner.reason: History and issue participation connect this person most directly to the existing subagent concurrency resolver and lane behavior.
